pillar_reactions.evidence: The mobility component was reinforced rather than presented fresh, and the prospect revealed he had no idea what it was: 'I don't know if you're already doing a mobility routine at the moment.' 'No, I don't even know what that is.' He then followed up on the live workouts twice - 'I never quite understood the live workout on Thursday, what exactly does that mean?' and 'is that something that I would watch, or could I watch and actually do it?' - and on whether a beginner could keep up.
Nutrition was not raised at all on this call. It may have been covered on the Monday call, which is not in this batch.

Presented in its reduced group form - post questions in the community, Trevor and Kate respond, film yourself for form feedback, Thursday live workouts - with the limitation stated plainly: 'of course it's not like how it would be with one-on-one coaching.' His reaction was to probe who would actually be there for him: 'my only contact with you guys has been you. So now moving forward, I no longer will be talking to you?'

anchors.raw: that will give me an opportunity to do the program. And save, you know, save some considerable amount of money, which I need for other things that are popping up
anchors.note: The stated reason for choosing the $1,000 tier over the one-to-one offer was liquidity, not doubt about the coaching. A retired 68-year-old with other expenses coming up is exactly the profile the stated ICP's income criterion is meant to screen, and he still bought - just five sixths cheaper.

anchors.raw: I know that I saw one of his videos and he says this is the recommended beginner workout. And so my intention is to do that workout again today.
anchors.note: He had already started training off free content before paying anything, and was tracking it himself in a spreadsheet he built. The second appearance in this batch of Primal's own free content functioning as a credible substitute - though here it converted rather than blocked, because the free version hurt him.

anchors.raw: I did probably the workout that Trevor's going to recommend for week one. And I ran through seven rounds. Yeah, in 27 minutes, I was dead.
anchors.note: He executed the programme before buying it, unprompted and to the point of injury. Intent was never the issue on this deal; capacity to pay and physical capacity were.

unmet_demand.want: Form correction. A 68-year-old beginner with lingering injuries who has already hurt his knees and back needs someone watching him move.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He bought the tier that explicitly excludes one-to-one. The substitute offered was filming himself and posting into a community for Trevor or Kate to respond, with the limitation acknowledged on the call - 'of course it's not like how it would be with one-on-one coaching.' The prospect who most needs supervision bought the product with the least of it.

unmet_demand.want: A continuing human relationship with the company - he asked directly whether he would lose his only contact
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The $1,000 product does not include a named person. The gap was filled informally and personally by the rep promising to text every two to three weeks from his own WhatsApp, which is goodwill rather than a product feature and does not survive him leaving the role.

unmet_demand.want: Written workout and progress tracking - he had built his own spreadsheet and hoped he would not have to: 'I hope I'll get this from you guys in writing, so I don't have to write it down'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Actually served - the rep screen-shared the tracking sheets and promised to email them ahead of access. Recorded only because he had to build his own first and did not know they existed.
